parsed.explanation: Federal layer is traveller-facing and hostile: binary sex definition, no X/self-selected markers on passports or visas, visa cable instructing refusal where sex is in doubt with possible lifetime fraud ineligibility, passports reportedly confiscated/blocked, multiple foreign travel advisories issued, and an executive order barring trans people from government-funded single-sex facilities. Immigration custody documents beatings, forced labour, solitary and sexual abuse of trans detainees. Division layer adds a gender-affirming-care ban for under-18s with provider liability and a private right of sue, plus a high raw count of anti-LGBTQ incidents.

entry_documents.exposure: Federal EO defines binary sex, ends X/new self-selected markers; visa cable directs refusal where records cast doubt on sex and invites consideration of lifetime fraud ineligibility; travellers report confiscated/blocked passports; 8+ foreign governments issued advisories. Status: documented.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X-marker passports valid to expiry; challenges pending in national courts; Supreme Court allowed restrictions Nov 2025. Status: documented.
entry_documents.interaction: Division's X driver's-licence marker and post-2018 accommodations law do not reach federally issued visas or entry screening; state generosity is bypassed at the border. Status: documented.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Immigration custody documents trans men subjected to forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement and severe sexual abuse; federal corrections adopted conversion-therapy-style policies (hair cut, hormones removed) from 2026 and stopped reporting trans prisoner counts. Status: documented.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Functioning state courts; national hate-crime statute; no documented federal remedy for detained trans visitors. Status: uncertain.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Document discrepancy or visa refusal → immigration custody → documented abuse pathway; state civil-rights remedies do not reach federal custody. Status: documented.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Federal EO bars trans people from government-funded single-sex facilities (airports, federal buildings, parks) — a continuous universal exposure. Division's own facility status not documented on the map. Status: documented federally, uncertain division-wide.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Division public-accommodation protections since 2018/2020; state high court protected trans students 3-1 in Aug 2024. Status: documented.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: State accommodation protections do not override federal facility rules in federally funded settings; the trespass statute cited belongs to a different unit. Status: documented.

care_services.exposure: Division bans gender-affirming medicine (July 2024) and blockers/hormones/chest surgery for under-18s (Aug 2025, effective Jan 2026) with provider discipline and a right to sue; federal proposal bars insurance reimbursement for under-18 care; DOJ subpoenaed under-19 patient records. Status: documented.
care_services.protection: Adult care not banned; public-insurance transition coverage restored 2017; conversion therapy banned since 2019. Status: documented.
care_services.interaction: A family travelling with a trans minor faces care denial, provider liability and guardian investigation — the parent need not be the defendant. Status: documented.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Federal EO calls care for minors 'mutilation,' directs law enforcement to investigate schools; counterterrorism strategy targets 'radically pro-transgender' groups; advocates compare trajectory to early genocide stages. Dossier notes ideology is not itself a reward criterion. Status: documented.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: National hate-crime statute; division panic defence abolished 2024, hate-crime enhancements 2019, civil-rights act enforced (July 2026 ruling for a struck trans woman). Status: documented.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Federal threat-framing raises outing severity while division enforcement offers real recourse for street assault — not for federal custody or entry. Status: documented.

minors_guardians.exposure: Division care bans with provider liability and private right of sue; sports ban (eligibility by birth certificate, stayed, current status unknown); federal EO criminally targets teachers facilitating social transition; parents may opt out of gender-identity instruction. Status: documented.
minors_guardians.protection: State high court protected trans students Aug 2024; 2022 student-gender-disclosure bill failed; conversion-therapy ban upheld (2022 repeal attempt died). Status: documented.
minors_guardians.interaction: Travelling guardian's child could be denied care and the family exposed to state inquiry; federal school-prosecution policy applies if the minor enrols. Status: documented.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: 2025 census recorded 72 anti-LGBTQ incidents (2nd-highest raw count; no denominator, so no rate established); encyclopedia calls division 'least safe in region' for trans citizens — attributed, not measured. Status: documented.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Civil-rights statute covers housing/employment/public accommodations since 2018, health/jury 2020, schools 2019; hate-crime enhancements 2019; 2022 poll: 88% support protections; documented July 2026 court win. Status: documented.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Strong division recourse mitigates street and service hostility but does not reach federal entry, facilities or custody. Status: documented.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Passport challenge unresolved; Supreme Court allowed restrictions; several EOs enjoined but in flux; sports-ban and care-ban injunction status unknown; equality map warns unmapped sex-definition laws may still apply. Status: documented/uncertain.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Legal-aid FAQ on passport rules; pending civil-liberties suit; functioning division courts with recorded pro-trans rulings. Status: documented.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Practical exposure varies by which measures are operative on travel dates, and federal remedies, if any, are unproven. Status: uncertain.

anchor_checks.comparison: Saruth combines border detention with assaults, withheld medical care, delayed habeas and likely punishment for complaining — remedies illusory. This dossier documents severe immigration-custody abuse but no execution pathway, no blanket identity entry bar, working division courts and documented pro-trans rulings, so it sits well above 0.15.

Drellia's universal registration/hotel database, repeated interviews and slow ombuds mirror this dossier's universal federal document/facility exposure. But this division adds enforced accommodations law, hate-crime penalties, an 88% supportive poll and a 2026 civil-rights conviction — real operative recourse — placing it somewhat above 0.45.

Vellmaris shows a document-mismatch stop cured by national equality law, intervention, apology and compensation with courts reliably releasing. Here the federal document regime is itself the exposure, upheld at the highest level, plus a documented custody-abuse record — so remedies do not neutralise the state's own conduct; below 0.65.

Norathia recognises trans passports, trains officers, provides counsel and tribunal-ordered releases. This jurisdiction does the opposite federally — marker restrictions, refusal cable, facility exclusion — so despite strong division protections it falls materially below the 0.85 tier.

parsed.synthesis: Two regimes interact. The division operates genuine, enforced protections: accommodations coverage since 2018, hate-crime enhancements, panic-defence abolition, a protected-students ruling and a 2026 civil-rights conviction, backed by 88% public support — low street and service exposure. The federal layer governs the journey stages that matter most: entry, visa documents encoding binary sex with refusal and lifetime-ineligibility exposure, government-funded facilities exclusion, and immigration custody with documented abuse of trans detainees. The division cannot offset these; it only softens what happens after entry on private and state ground. A care ban with provider liability and right to sue makes the family/minor case materially worse than the solo-adult case. Ongoing litigation keeps outcomes date-dependent. Net: functioning protections at one level, hostile universal exposures at the other — elevated risk overall.
